passages.heading: 6.1. Why Sub-Agents Disagree
passages.text: Different specialization frames. A sub-agent on legal strategy may recommend X; a sub-agent on case management may recommend Y. Each is correct within its frame.

passages.heading: 6.1. Why Sub-Agents Disagree
passages.text: Different evidence weights. A sub-agent may weight recent case law heavily; another may weight long-established methodology more. Both are reasonable choices that produce different recommendations.

passages.heading: 6.1. Why Sub-Agents Disagree
passages.text: These disagreements often contain the most important information the principal needs. A composite agent that resolved them silently would hide what the principal most needs to see.

passages.heading: 6.2. Surfacing Versus Resolving
passages.text: This is critical because: - Algorithmic resolution would impose hidden judgment on the principal - Resolution loses information that the disagreement contains - The principal's authority over their work depends on access to underlying disagreement - Profession-level differences in approach should remain visible, not be smoothed away

passages.heading: 6.3. Presentation of Disagreement
passages.text: Pattern 1 — Side-by-side recommendation. "Sub-agent A recommends X with reasoning ... ; sub-agent B recommends Y with reasoning ... ." Principal sees both directly.

passages.heading: 6.3. Presentation of Disagreement
passages.text: Pattern 2 — Common ground first. "Both sub-agents agree that base position . They differ on specific issue : A says X; B says Y." Helps principal see what is settled and what is contested.

passages.heading: 6.3. Presentation of Disagreement
passages.text: Pattern 3 — Compatibility analysis. "A's recommendation may produce result X. B's recommendation may produce result Y. The choice depends on whether you prioritize Z." Helps principal see what the disagreement actually means for outcomes.

passages.heading: 6.3. Presentation of Disagreement
passages.text: Pattern 4 — Resolution suggestion without execution . "If you favor X, here's how A's recommendation can be implemented. If you favor Y, here's how B's." Principal still chooses; the agent helps with implementation of the chosen direction.

passages.heading: 6.3. Presentation of Disagreement
passages.text: What does not work: averaging, voting, "balanced" outputs that mask the underlying disagreement. These appear neutral but actually impose hidden judgment.

passages.heading: 6.4. When the Principal Cannot Decide
passages.text: Escalation to mentor. If the principal has access to a human mentor, the composite agent can structure the disagreement for mentor review.

passages.heading: 6.4. When the Principal Cannot Decide
passages.text: Risk-weighted default. If one recommendation is more conservative smaller commitment, easier reversal , the composite agent can suggest defaulting to that while gathering more information.

passages.heading: 6.4. When the Principal Cannot Decide
passages.text: Acknowledged uncertainty. Sometimes the right output is: "You face a genuine professional judgment call here. Here's what each sub-agent recommends; here's what's at stake; this is a moment where your accumulated experience matters."

passages.heading: 6.5. Learning from Resolution
passages.text: - Which sub-agents the principal tends to follow when there's disagreement - Which contexts predict which choice - Whether the principal's choices show evolving patterns

passages.heading: 6.5. Learning from Resolution
passages.text: This information should be available to the principal their own pattern of decisions over time but not used to hide future disagreements. The point is not to predict and pre-resolve; the point is to give the principal insight into their own practice.

passages.heading: 6.5. Learning from Resolution

passages.heading: 7.1. Cost Structure
passages.text: Sub-agent development : substantial fixed cost per sub-agent. A high-quality narrow-specialist sub-agent might cost €50,000- €500,000 to build, depending on knowledge base depth.

passages.heading: 7.1. Cost Structure
passages.text: Coordinator operation : low marginal cost per principal. LLM API costs scale with use, but the coordinator itself doesn't require per-principal customization beyond configuration.

passages.heading: 7.1. Cost Structure
passages.text: This produces interesting unit economics. If an ecosystem has 500 sub-agents and 10,000 principals, the ratio of sub-agent fixed cost to total user value is highly favorable.

passages.heading: 7.2. Combinatorial Value
passages.text: The number of possible configurations grows combinatorially: - 100 sub-agents, choose 15: ~250 billion possible configurations - 500 sub-agents, choose 20: astronomical

passages.heading: 7.2. Combinatorial Value
passages.text: In practice, configurations cluster around common patterns. But even within any profession, there's room for substantial diversity. Each principal's configuration genuinely reflects their distinctive practice.

passages.heading: 7.2. Combinatorial Value
passages.text: The combinatorial value is the central economic insight: a relatively small fixed investment in sub-agent development unlocks an essentially unlimited space of unique principal configurations.

passages.heading: 7.3. Investment Strategy
passages.text: Phase 1 : Build a small set of broadly applicable sub-agents perhaps 20-50 covering core specializations of one profession . This requires substantial upfront investment but enables initial configurations.

passages.heading: 7.3. Investment Strategy
passages.text: Phase 2 : Expand to more specialized sub-agents based on observed configuration gaps. As principals use the system, their requests for specializations not yet available drive priority for new sub-agent development.

passages.heading: 7.3. Investment Strategy
passages.text: Phase 3 : Federation with external sub-agent providers. Once the registry framework is established, sub-agents from other organizations can be integrated, accelerating coverage.

passages.heading: 7.3. Investment Strategy
passages.text: Phase 4 : Cross-profession expansion. Sub-agents developed for one profession may apply to adjacent professions. Methodology sub-agents particularly cross professional boundaries.

passages.heading: 7.3. Investment Strategy
passages.text: This phasing parallels how academic libraries develop: starting with core texts, expanding to specialized works, federating with other libraries, and enabling cross-disciplinary access.

passages.heading: 7.4. Funding Models for Sub-Agent Development
passages.text: Hybrid. Most realistic for early-stage ecosystem. Foundation funds core infrastructure, sponsors fund priority sub-agents, practitioners contribute to specific narrow sub-agents through volunteer expert work.

passages.heading: 7.5. Sustainable Economics for the SGB Pilot
passages.text: Instead of building one large profession-wide agent for German social law, build: - 20-30 narrow sub-agents covering core SGB specializations - A coordinator that practitioners configure individually - Templates for common practice patterns general advocacy, disability rights, elderly care, mental health, child welfare

passages.heading: 7.5. Sustainable Economics for the SGB Pilot
passages.text: Estimated investment: - 20 sub-agents at €50K average: €1,000,000 - Coordinator development: €300,000 - First-year operations: €200,000 - Total Year 1: €1.5 million

passages.heading: 7.5. Sustainable Economics for the SGB Pilot
passages.text: This is higher than the original estimate €430K but produces substantially more capability. Practitioners get composite configurations matching their specific practice, not a generic SGB agent.

passages.heading: 7.5. Sustainable Economics for the SGB Pilot
passages.text: For 1,000 practitioners over three years, this comes to approximately €500/practitioner/year — feasible for foundation funding or modest practitioner contribution.

passages.heading: 7.5. Sustainable Economics for the SGB Pilot

passages.heading: 8. Seven Domains of Application
passages.text: Composite Skills Agents apply naturally to professions where practice typically combines specializations. We identify seven domains where the pattern fits especially well.

passages.heading: 8.1. Domain 1 — Music Education and Performance
passages.text: Sub-agent specializations might include : Classical composition, jazz improvisation, electronic music production, specific instruments piano, violin, voice, etc. , genres folk traditions, contemporary, baroque , pedagogy children, adults, beginners, advanced , technical skills music theory, ear training, sight-reading , accompanying disciplines audio engineering, music history, ethnomusicology .

passages.heading: 8.1. Domain 1 — Music Education and Performance
passages.text: Typical configurations : A jazz pianist who teaches has different needs from a classical violinist, who has different needs from an electronic music producer. Each builds their own configuration from the available sub-agents.

passages.heading: 8.1. Domain 1 — Music Education and Performance
passages.text: Existing analog : This pattern is already embodied in how musicians actually train — studying with multiple teachers in different specialties — but no AI infrastructure currently supports it.

passages.heading: 8.2. Domain 2 — Visual and Creative Arts
passages.text: Sub-agent specializations might include : Drawing fundamentals, painting techniques, digital illustration, animation, sculpture, photography, color theory, composition, art history by period or movement , specific tools Adobe Creative Suite, Procreate, Blender , business skills gallery work, commission management, intellectual property .

passages.heading: 8.2. Domain 2 — Visual and Creative Arts
passages.text: Typical configurations : A digital illustrator who also does traditional sketching and runs a small business has very different needs from a fine arts painter focused on gallery representation.

passages.heading: 8.2. Domain 2 — Visual and Creative Arts
passages.text: Bridge to existing infrastructure : Many artists already combine multiple educational sources online courses, traditional training, peer learning . Composite agents formalize and augment this practice.

passages.heading: 8.3. Domain 3 — Specialized Legal Practice
passages.text: Sub-agent specializations might include : Specific area of law social, criminal, family, immigration , procedural expertise specific courts, jurisdictions , client population elderly, disabled, immigrants, children , language German, English, Russian, etc. , technical skills drafting, oral advocacy, negotiation , supporting fields medical understanding, psychological assessment .

passages.heading: 8.3. Domain 3 — Specialized Legal Practice
passages.text: Typical configurations : A lawyer specializing in disability rights for migrants speaks both German and the migrant's language and has medical understanding for assessing claims — a combination requiring multiple sub-agents.

passages.heading: 8.4. Domain 4 — Medical Practice with Multiple Specialties
passages.text: Sub-agent specializations might include : Specific organ systems, types of conditions acute, chronic, infectious, autoimmune , patient populations pediatric, geriatric, prenatal , specialized procedures, diagnostic interpretation radiology, lab work, pathology , specific subspecialties rheumatology, immunology, infectious diseases .

passages.heading: 8.4. Domain 4 — Medical Practice with Multiple Specialties
passages.text: Typical configurations : A primary care physician working in a rural clinic with elderly patients faces different challenges from a specialist working in tertiary care. Even within specialties, working with specific patient populations requires different configurations.

passages.heading: 8.4. Domain 4 — Medical Practice with Multiple Specialties
passages.text: Critical caveat : Medical configurations require especially rigorous quality assurance and explicit boundaries around what the composite agent can support.

passages.heading: 8.5. Domain 5 — Technical Architecture and Engineering
passages.text: Sub-agent specializations might include : Programming languages, architecture patterns, deployment platforms, security disciplines, performance engineering, testing approaches, specific application domains fintech, medtech, e-commerce, infrastructure , compliance regimes.

passages.heading: 8.5. Domain 5 — Technical Architecture and Engineering
passages.text: Typical configurations : An engineer specializing in high-performance distributed systems for medical applications needs specific combinations: distributed systems, performance engineering, plus medical compliance, plus security requirements specific to healthcare.

passages.heading: 8.5. Domain 5 — Technical Architecture and Engineering
passages.text: Bridge to existing tools : Many engineering teams already informally combine specialist resources Stack Overflow, language-specific documentation, specialist consultants . Composite agents formalize this.

passages.heading: 8.6. Domain 6 — Academic Research and Cross-Disciplinary Work
passages.text: Sub-agent specializations might include : Specific methodologies quantitative, qualitative, mixed methods , research traditions, statistical approaches, computational methods, writing conventions for specific journals or fields, literature search across databases, ethical frameworks.

passages.heading: 8.6. Domain 6 — Academic Research and Cross-Disciplinary Work
passages.text: Typical configurations : A computational biologist working on epidemiology with humanities co-authors faces unique configuration needs combining biology, computer science, epidemiological methods, and humanities perspectives.

passages.heading: 8.7. Domain 7 — Therapeutic Practice and Mental Health
passages.text: Sub-agent specializations might include : Therapeutic modalities CBT, somatic experiencing, narrative therapy, gestalt , specific conditions trauma, addiction, eating disorders, mood disorders , client populations children, adolescents, elderly, couples, groups , supporting frameworks neuroscience, attachment theory, family systems , cultural competencies, specific skills crisis intervention, grou

passages.heading: 8.7. Domain 7 — Therapeutic Practice and Mental Health
passages.text: Typical configurations : A therapist working with adolescents who have eating disorders in immigrant families requires specific combinations spanning therapeutic modalities, developmental psychology, eating disorder specifics, and cultural competency.

passages.heading: 8.7. Domain 7 — Therapeutic Practice and Mental Health
passages.text: Critical caveat : Mental health practice requires especially careful attention to where AI support is appropriate research, documentation, knowledge lookup versus where it is not clinical judgment, therapeutic relationship . Composite agents operate strictly in the support role.

passages.heading: 8.8. Pattern Across Domains
passages.text: What unites these domains: - Practice is deeply specialized, but specialization combines rather than replaces general profession competency - Practitioners typically span 10-30 distinct specializations - Each specialization is shared with other practitioners but configurations are individually distinctive - Existing professional development already follows this pattern; composite agents formalize

passages.heading: 8.8. Pattern Across Domains
passages.text: The pattern is general. We expect Composite Skills Agents to become standard infrastructure across most skilled professions within 5-10 years.

passages.heading: 9.1. Connection to Pattern Library
passages.text: The Nautilus pattern library architecture public patterns, private instances, anonymization pipeline provides foundational support for the sub-agent registry. Patterns become source material for sub-agents. Anonymized practitioner contributions flow into pattern library, which informs sub-agent updates.

passages.heading: 9.1. Connection to Pattern Library
passages.text: The connection is not just analogical. The same infrastructure serves both: - Pattern library: knowledge fragments accessible to humans for review - Sub-agent registry: knowledge fragments operationalized into AI assistants

passages.heading: 9.2. Connection to Guild Structure
passages.text: OKWF's guild structure groups of practitioners by professional area provides natural organization for sub-agent development. Each guild can: - Identify priority sub-agents for their area - Contribute expert curation - Test sub-agents in actual practice - Maintain quality standards - Develop common configuration templates

passages.heading: 9.3. Connection to Double-Triangle Architecture
passages.text: In the Double-Triangle Architecture, each Node human practitioner has lower-triangle assistants supporting their work. Composite Skills Agents formalize what lower-triangle assistants typically contain: not one undifferentiated assistant but a coordinated configuration of narrow specialists.

passages.heading: 9.3. Connection to Double-Triangle Architecture
passages.text: The composite agent itself is the orchestrator of the lower triangle. The sub-agents in the configuration are the actual "lower triangle assistants" doing specialized work.

passages.heading: 9.4. Connection to Representative Agents
passages.text: Composite Skills Agents and Representative Agents work together naturally: - The composite agent supports the practitioner's work - The representative agent supports the practitioner's external position

passages.heading: 9.4. Connection to Representative Agents
passages.text: A mature practitioner has both: composite for daily work, representative for opportunity navigation. They share underlying profile information about the practitioner but operate in different layers.

passages.heading: 9.5. Refined OKWF Rollout Plan
passages.text: Phase 0 Months 1-12 : Foundation establishment, initial sub-agent set for one profession perhaps SGB social law . Build 20-30 narrow sub-agents plus coordinator. Pilot with 5-10 practitioners.

passages.heading: 9.5. Refined OKWF Rollout Plan
passages.text: Phase 1 Year 2 : Expand sub-agent set, scale practitioners to 100-500. Establish pattern library connection, anonymization pipeline. Begin contribution flow back into sub-agent updates.

passages.heading: 9.5. Refined OKWF Rollout Plan
passages.text: Phase 2 Years 2-3 : Expand to second profession perhaps educational support for disabled students, maintaining thematic connection . Cross-profession integration of methodology sub-agents.

passages.heading: 9.5. Refined OKWF Rollout Plan
passages.text: Phase 3 Years 3-5 : Multiple professions, federated sub-agent registry, mature configuration management. Begin adding Representative Agent layer for principals who want it.

passages.heading: 9.5. Refined OKWF Rollout Plan
passages.text: This plan is more realistic than the earlier proposal because it matches how skilled practitioners actually develop and what they actually need.

passages.heading: 9.6. Practical Implication for Pilot Design
passages.text: Cost increases €1.5M vs €430K for Year 1 , but produces a genuinely useful infrastructure that scales to multiple adjacent legal domains and supports practitioners' actual diverse practices rather than forcing one-size-fits-all generalization.

passages.heading: 9.6. Practical Implication for Pilot Design
passages.text: This is a better proposal for foundation funders even at higher cost, because it demonstrates a more sophisticated understanding of how skilled practice works and produces infrastructure with broader applicability.

passages.heading: 10.1. Risk: Configuration Paralysis
passages.text: Scenario : Faced with hundreds of available sub-agents, the principal cannot decide which to include. Configuration becomes overwhelming task. Principal gives up and uses generic Professional Colleague Agent instead, missing the value of composite.

passages.heading: 10.1. Risk: Configuration Paralysis
passages.text: Mitigations : - Strong starting templates for common professional patterns - AI-assisted recommendation as default with override - Limit on initial configuration size start with 5-10, grow over time - Mentor connection for complex configuration decisions

passages.heading: 10.2. Risk: Configuration Echo Chamber
passages.text: Scenario : Principal selects sub-agents that confirm their existing approach, missing specializations that would challenge or expand their practice. Composite becomes a sophisticated form of confirmation bias.

passages.heading: 10.2. Risk: Configuration Echo Chamber
passages.text: Mitigations : - Recommendation system explicitly suggests "growth-edge" sub-agents outside principal's current configuration - Regular configuration reviews with prompts to consider unfamiliar specializations - Mentor input that intentionally surfaces alternative perspectives - Public visibility of how others in the same profession configure differently

passages.heading: 10.3. Risk: Sub-Agent Dependency
passages.text: Scenario : Principal becomes dependent on a specific sub-agent that is later deprecated or significantly changed. Their practice disrupts when configuration needs to change.

passages.heading: 10.3. Risk: Sub-Agent Dependency
passages.text: Mitigations : - Open standards make sub-agents portable and replaceable - Multiple sub-agents covering same specialization compete on quality, not lock-in - Notification when sub-agent will be deprecated, with migration paths - Configuration export so principal can move between coordinator providers

passages.heading: 10.4. Risk: Coordinator Bias
passages.text: Scenario : The coordinator general infrastructure managing configurations develops biases in routing or synthesis that systematically favor some sub-agents over others. Practice patterns shift in ways principals didn't choose.

passages.heading: 10.4. Risk: Coordinator Bias
passages.text: Mitigations : - Open coordinator architecture, with multiple coordinator options - Transparent routing logic principal can see why sub-agent was selected - Auditable behavior over time - Coordinator evaluation as part of platform governance

passages.heading: 10.5. Risk: Quality Variation Across Sub-Agents
passages.text: Scenario : Sub-agent registry includes high-quality and low-quality sub-agents. Principals using lower-quality sub-agents in their configurations get poorer support without realizing it.

passages.heading: 10.5. Risk: Quality Variation Across Sub-Agents
passages.text: Mitigations : - Visible quality indicators on sub-agents - Curation standards for inclusion in main registry - User feedback loops affecting visibility - Federated curation allowing principals to choose which curators they trust

passages.heading: 10.6. Risk: Profession Fragmentation
passages.text: Scenario : As composite configurations diversify, professional practice fragments. Practitioners working on similar problems develop incompatible approaches because they used different sub-agent configurations. Professional coherence weakens.

passages.heading: 10.6. Risk: Profession Fragmentation
passages.text: Mitigations : - Sub-agents share common foundational knowledge so configurations diverge from a common base - Guild structure maintains profession-level community across diverse configurations - Cross-configuration patterns in shared pattern library - Recognition that some fragmentation is healthy diversification versus unhealthy disconnection

passages.heading: 10.7. Risk: Hidden Dependencies Among Sub-Agents
passages.text: Scenario : A configuration appears to work well, but its output depends on subtle interactions between specific sub-agents. When one sub-agent updates, the configuration's output changes in ways neither principal nor coordinator anticipated.

passages.heading: 10.7. Risk: Hidden Dependencies Among Sub-Agents
passages.text: Mitigations : - Version pinning configurations specify exact sub-agent versions, opt into updates - Compatibility testing when sub-agents update - Notification of significant behavioral changes in sub-agents - Configuration testing against past examples to detect drift

passages.heading: 10.8. Risk: Configuration as Competitive Advantage Hoarding
passages.text: Scenario : Principals discover that specific configurations are particularly effective. They keep these configurations secret as competitive advantage. Configuration knowledge becomes hoarded rather than shared, limiting benefit to broader practice.

passages.heading: 10.8. Risk: Configuration as Competitive Advantage Hoarding
passages.text: Mitigations : - Default openness about configurations shared by default, opt-in to keep private - Anonymized configuration patterns published in pattern library - Recognition for sharing effective configurations - Cooperative ownership models that align individual benefit with collective improvement

passages.heading: 11.1. Granularity Questions
passages.text: How narrow should sub-agents be? Too narrow and configurations become unmanageable; too broad and the composite pattern collapses back to Professional Colleague Agent.

passages.heading: 11.1. Granularity Questions
passages.text: What's the right granularity for different professions? Likely varies — music might support finer granularity than law. Empirical question requiring deployment.

passages.heading: 11.2. Configuration Stability
passages.text: How often should principals revise configurations? Too often and they spend more time configuring than working; too rarely and configurations drift from current practice.

passages.heading: 11.2. Configuration Stability
passages.text: What signals suggest configuration revision is needed? Likely some combination of: significant change in principal's work, new sub-agents available, observed gaps in current configuration, explicit annual review.

passages.heading: 11.3. Cross-Professional Configurations
passages.text: When practitioners genuinely span professions lawyer who is also social worker, doctor who is also researcher , can their configuration span sub-agents from multiple professions? How does the coordinator handle this?

passages.heading: 11.4. Configuration Evolution at Scale
passages.text: If 10,000 practitioners use composite agents, what happens across the population? Do configurations cluster around patterns? Does this clustering match natural sub-specialties or create artificial groupings?

passages.heading: 11.5. Sub-Agent Quality Across Cultures
passages.text: Sub-agents developed primarily in one cultural or linguistic context may not serve well in others. How does the registry handle cultural variation? Multiple parallel sub-agents for different contexts? Configurable cultural overlays?

passages.heading: 11.6. Liability for Composite Outputs
passages.text: When a composite agent's output drawing on multiple sub-agents contains errors, who bears responsibility? The principal who used it? The coordinator? Each sub-agent that contributed? The platform?

passages.heading: 11.7. The "Emergence" Question
passages.text: When many sub-agents combine in a configuration, do useful properties emerge that weren't present in any individual sub-agent? Or do composite outputs simply average their contributions?

passages.heading: 11.8. Transition from Composite to Representative
passages.text: As principals develop sophisticated composite configurations, when if ever does it make sense to graduate to a Representative Agent Type 4 with truly individual specialization? Or do composites serve indefinitely?

passages.heading: 12.1. For Practitioners
passages.text: Tell us how your practice combines specializations. What configuration of sub-agents would actually serve your work? What would make composite agents valuable versus merely complex?

passages.heading: 12.2. For Curators and Domain Experts
passages.text: Sub-agent registry development needs curated knowledge across many narrow specializations. Domain experts willing to help develop sub-agents in their specialties — particularly compensated through foundation funding — would substantially accelerate deployment.

passages.heading: 12.3. For Software Engineers and Architects
passages.text: Coordinator infrastructure is substantial engineering work. Open-source contributions to reference implementations welcome. Particular needs: - Sub-agent registry standards and protocols - Configuration management interfaces - Disagreement detection and presentation systems - Audit and observability tools

passages.heading: 12.4. For Researchers
passages.text: Empirical studies of composite configuration patterns would illuminate questions raised in Section 11. Particular value in: - Configuration clustering analysis - Effectiveness comparison: composite vs. monolithic agents - Long-term effects on professional development - Cross-cultural deployment outcomes

passages.heading: 12.5. For Foundation Funders
passages.text: Composite Skills Agents represent higher-leverage infrastructure investment than monolithic Professional Colleague Agents: - More flexible support across diverse practitioner needs - More scalable across adjacent professions - More aligned with how mastery actually develops - More resilient to changes in any single component

passages.heading: 12.6. For Policymakers
passages.text: Regulatory frameworks for AI in professional practice will need to address composite architectures specifically. Questions about liability, professional responsibility, and quality standards apply differently when many specialized sub-agents contribute to outputs.

passages.heading: 13. Closing
passages.text: Mastery in skilled work has always been composite. The yoga master who studied with twenty teachers did not invent his practice from nothing; he combined what he learned from specialists. The musician, the lawyer, the physician, the architect, the therapist — all develop their distinctive practice by combining individually general skills into individually distinctive configurations.

passages.heading: 13. Closing
passages.text: What is new is the possibility of AI infrastructure that mirrors this structure. Until now, AI support for skilled work has been either too generic one assistant for everyone or too custom unique development per principal . Neither matches how practitioners actually develop and operate.

passages.heading: 13. Closing
passages.text: Composite Skills Agents fill this gap. They make the twenty-teacher pattern accessible at scale: any practitioner can configure their own ensemble of specialist sub-agents, creating support that matches their actual practice rather than forcing them into pre-defined categories.

passages.heading: 13. Closing
passages.text: This recognition changes the practical strategy for AI deployment in professions. Building monolithic profession-wide agents serves narrow purposes well but cannot serve the more common case of practitioners with distinctive specialized configurations. Building uniquely customized agents serves deep representational needs but cannot scale.

passages.heading: 13. Closing
passages.text: Building composite infrastructure — registry of narrow sub-agents plus configurable coordinators — serves the broad middle where most skilled practice actually happens.

passages.heading: 13. Closing
passages.text: For the Open Knowledge Work Foundation specifically, composite infrastructure provides: - More flexible support for diverse practitioner needs - Stronger alignment with mission of empowering distinctive practitioners - Better economic structure combinatorial leverage of fixed investment - More natural connection to existing pattern library architecture - Clearer migration path from initial pilot t

passages.heading: 13. Closing
passages.text: The question is whether we build it carefully — with open standards, foundation governance, quality curation, and practitioner ownership — or whether we let it emerge through commercial dynamics that favor concentration over distribution.

passages.heading: Acknowledgments
passages.text: The Composite Skills Agent concept emerged from dialogue with Claude Anthropic on April 26, 2026. The crystallizing contribution was the user's observation that the binary view between Professional Colleague Agent Type 1 and Representative Agent Type 4 missed the most common middle case — practitioners whose distinctive value comes from combining individually general specializations.

passages.heading: Acknowledgments
passages.text: The metaphor of the Indian yoga master who studied with twenty teachers, drawn from a journalist's interview the user remembered, provides the central illustration that makes the pattern clear.

passages.text: Это очень тонкое и важное наблюдение. Вы заметили нечто, что в шестой статье было упрощено — будто между Профессиональным Коллегой-Агентом стандартизированная профессия и Представительским Агентом уникальный индивидум существует чистый разрыв. На самом деле там целый спектр.

passages.heading: Claude hat geantwortet: Это очень тонкое и важное наблюдение.
passages.text: История, которую вы привели, имеет глубокий смысл. Двадцать один учитель, каждый со своей узкой специализацией. Двадцать первый из них синтезирует уникальную комбинацию из учений первых двадцати. И эта комбинация именно его — не его учителей по отдельности, и не «среднего йога».

passages.heading: Claude hat geantwortet: Это очень тонкое и важное наблюдение.
passages.text: Это не редкая структура. Это базовая структура мастерства в любой сложной области. Музыкант, который учился у пианиста, у композитора, у дирижёра, у звукоинженера, у джазового импровизатора — становится уникальным именно через комбинацию, не через одно из этих направлений.

passages.heading: Claude hat geantwortet: Это очень тонкое и важное наблюдение.
passages.text: Юрист, который работал в корпоративном праве, потом в правах потребителей, потом в технологическом праве — приносит уникальную перспективу, которая не существует ни у одного из его предыдущих наставников.

passages.heading: Claude hat geantwortet: Это очень тонкое и важное наблюдение.
passages.text: Но реальный мир работает иначе. Большинство профессионалов не на полюсах. Они в промежуточной зоне: имеют профессиональную базу плюс уникальный набор специализаций, который делает их особенными среди коллег по профессии.

passages.heading: Claude hat geantwortet: Это очень тонкое и важное наблюдение.
passages.text: Учитель литературы, который специализируется на современной поэзии и феминистских интерпретациях. Не «уникальный единственный в мире» это слишком высокая планка , но и не «типичный учитель литературы». Что-то среднее.

passages.heading: Claude hat geantwortet: Это очень тонкое и важное наблюдение.
passages.text: Юрист по социальному праву, который специализируется на случаях, связанных с инвалидностью, и при этом имеет техническое образование. Не уникальный, но и не типичный.

passages.heading: Claude hat geantwortet: Это очень тонкое и важное наблюдение.
passages.text: Принципал имеет набор узких специализаций — допустим, восемь, или двенадцать, или двадцать. Не одну широкую профессию. Не уникальную идентичность. Набор.

passages.heading: Claude hat geantwortet: Это очень тонкое и важное наблюдение.

passages.heading: Это не Тип 1 — потому что профиль не общий для всей профессии. И это не Тип 4 — …
passages.text: Это не Тип 1 — потому что профиль не общий для всей профессии. И это не Тип 4 — потому что под-агенты не уникальные для принципала, они общие.

passages.heading: Это не Тип 1 — потому что профиль не общий для всей профессии. И это не Тип 4 — …
passages.text: В технических терминах: вы предлагаете архитектуру mixture of experts, но не на уровне нейронной сети, а на уровне профессиональной идентичности.

passages.heading: Это не Тип 1 — потому что профиль не общий для всей профессии. И это не Тип 4 — …
passages.text: Каждый под-агент — это, по сути, Профессиональный Коллега-Агент для своей узкой подспециальности. Композитный агент — это оркестратор этого набора, конфигурированного именно для этого учителя.

passages.heading: Это не Тип 1 — потому что профиль не общий для всей профессии. И это не Тип 4 — …
passages.text: Другой учитель музыки имел бы другую конфигурацию — может быть, без джаза, но с этномузыкологией. Третий — с акцентом на детскую музыкальную педагогику.

passages.heading: Это не Тип 1 — потому что профиль не общий для всей профессии. И это не Тип 4 — …
passages.text: Каждый из двадцати обучающих учителей — это аналог узкоспециализированного Профессионального Коллеги-Агента. Они общедоступны. Любой ученик мог бы прийти к ним.

passages.heading: Это не Тип 1 — потому что профиль не общий для всей профессии. И это не Тип 4 — …
passages.text: С учётом этого вашего наблюдения, типология агентов на стороне принципала должна быть пересмотрена. Вместо пяти типов — шесть, и они образуют спектр от общего к уникальному:

passages.heading: Это не Тип 1 — потому что профиль не общий для всей профессии. И это не Тип 4 — …
passages.text: Тип 1.5 — Подспециализированный Коллега-Агент. Узкая специализация в профессии. Для всех адвокатов по социальному праву, не для всех юристов вообще.

passages.heading: Это не Тип 1 — потому что профиль не общий для всей профессии. И это не Тип 4 — …
passages.text: Тип 2 — Композитный Агент Навыков новый . Принципал имеет уникальный набор специализаций. Композитный агент координирует множество узкоспециализированных под-агентов под этот конкретный набор. Каждый под-агент общий, но сочетание уникально.

passages.heading: Это не Тип 1 — потому что профиль не общий для всей профессии. И это не Тип 4 — …
passages.text: Тип 1 Профессиональный Коллега работает только если профессия стандартизована достаточно, чтобы один общий шаблон был полезен. Учителя школы — да. Юристы — да. Но специалист по математической биологии с интересом к теории графов и опытом в эпидемиологии — нет. Никакой шаблон не покрывает эту комбинацию.

passages.heading: Это не Тип 1 — потому что профиль не общий для всей профессии. И это не Тип 4 — …
passages.text: Композитный Агент позволяет масштабироваться: вы инвестируете один раз в построение узкоспециализированных под-агентов теория графов, эпидемиология, математическая биология , и потом любой принципал может сконфигурировать свою уникальную комбинацию из существующих под-агентов.

passages.heading: Это не Тип 1 — потому что профиль не общий для всей профессии. И это не Тип 4 — …
passages.text: В шестой статье я писал, что Тип 1 имеет красивую экономику: одна инвестиция в профессиональный контекст, тысячи пользователей. Это всё ещё верно для Типа 1.

passages.heading: Это не Тип 1 — потому что профиль не общий для всей профессии. И это не Тип 4 — …
passages.text: Допустим, есть 100 узкоспециализированных под-агентов в области X. Каждый — отдельная инвестиция, но скромная узкая область, фокусированная база знаний .

passages.heading: Это не Тип 1 — потому что профиль не общий для всей профессии. И это не Тип 4 — …
passages.text: Это значит: каждая комбинация уникальна, но компоненты тиражируются. Принципал получает уникальную поддержку, но при этом платформа окупается за счёт совместного использования базовых компонентов.

passages.heading: Это не Тип 1 — потому что профиль не общий для всей профессии. И это не Тип 4 — …
passages.text: Учитель музыки. Базовая профессиональная подготовка плюс уникальные специализации. Композитный агент собирает под-агентов: по теории музыки, по конкретному инструменту, по детской педагогике, по конкретному жанру джаз, классика, фолк , по технологиям записи. Каждый учитель имеет свой набор. Никто не имеет всех ста.

passages.heading: Это не Тип 1 — потому что профиль не общий для всей профессии. И это не Тип 4 — …
passages.text: Юрист по социальному праву. Композитный агент: SGB IX, SGB XII, конкретные подспециализации инвалидность, психическое здоровье, дети, пожилые , процедурное право, конкретные земли Саксония, Бавария , интерфейс с медицинскими экспертизами. Юрист, специализирующийся на правах детей-инвалидов в Саксонии, имеет конкретную конфигурацию из набора.

passages.heading: Это не Тип 1 — потому что профиль не общий для всей профессии. И это не Тип 4 — …
passages.text: Врач общей практики. Композитный агент: каждая система органов как под-агент, плюс под-агенты по типичным сопутствующим заболеваниям, по гериатрии, по педиатрии, по конкретным редким состояниям, по интерпретации лабораторных тестов. Конкретный врач, работающий в основном с пожилыми пациентами в сельской местности, имеет свою конфигурацию.

passages.heading: Это не Тип 1 — потому что профиль не общий для всей профессии. И это не Тип 4 — …
passages.text: Программный архитектор. Композитный агент: по конкретным технологиям Python, Go, Rust , по архитектурным паттернам microservices, event-driven , по доменам финтех, медтех, e-commerce , по требованиям compliance, performance, accessibility . Архитектор, специализирующийся на разработке медицинских систем с фокусом на accessibility, имеет свой набор.

passages.heading: Это не Тип 1 — потому что профиль не общий для всей профессии. И это не Тип 4 — …
passages.text: Социальный работник. Композитный агент: по типу клиентов пожилые, дети, бездомные, мигранты , по типу проблем зависимости, психическое здоровье, домашнее насилие , по системам поддержки государственные, НКО, церковные , по правовым вопросам. Каждый социальный работник имеет свой набор по контексту своей работы.

passages.heading: Это не Тип 1 — потому что профиль не общий для всей профессии. И это не Тип 4 — …
passages.text: В каждой из этих профессий Тип 1 общий для профессии недостаточен — слишком много специализаций. Но Тип 5 уникальный для индивида избыточен — потому что узкие специализации общие, не уникальные. Композитный Агент — правильное решение.

passages.heading: Это не Тип 1 — потому что профиль не общий для всей профессии. И это не Тип 4 — …
passages.text: Реестр Узкоспециализированных Под-Агентов. Каталог всех существующих узкоспециализированных AI-помощников в данной экосистеме. Каждый под-агент имеет описание: какая специализация, какая глубина, какие границы.

passages.heading: Это не Тип 1 — потому что профиль не общий для всей профессии. И это не Тип 4 — …
passages.text: Процесс Конфигурирования Принципала. Помогает принципалу выбрать релевантные под-агенты из реестра. Может быть автоматическим анализ профиля принципала, рекомендации , полуавтоматическим диалог с принципалом , или ручным принципал выбирает сам .

passages.heading: Это не Тип 1 — потому что профиль не общий для всей профессии. И это не Тип 4 — …

passages.heading: Какой под-агент (или какие) должны её обработать
passages.text: Источник: MHTML‑снимок Вакансии в Anthropic по кластерам - Claude корень репозитория . Раздел диалога — 21 учитель индийского йога — спектр между Professional Colleague и Representative Agent.

passages.heading: Какой под-агент (или какие) должны её обработать
passages.text: Слой Эволюции. Со временем принципал может добавлять новые под-агенты в свою конфигурацию новые специализации появляются в его карьере или удалять специализации меняются .

passages.heading: Какой под-агент (или какие) должны её обработать
passages.text: Здесь интересно: эта архитектура очень близка к тому, что мы обсуждали для библиотеки паттернов в Nautilus и в концепт-документе OKWF.

passages.heading: Какой под-агент (или какие) должны её обработать
passages.text: Публичные паттерны = узкоспециализированные под-агенты. Приватные инстансы = конкретные конфигурации принципалов. Соединительные мосты между публичным и приватным = именно то, что Композитный Агент делает.

passages.heading: Какой под-агент (или какие) должны её обработать
passages.text: В концепт-документе OKWF мы обсуждали Pattern Library как механизм компаундирования знаний. Композитные Агенты — это активная форма этого pattern library. Не пассивная библиотека, к которой обращаются — а активный набор экспертов, к которым подключаются.

passages.heading: Какой под-агент (или какие) должны её обработать
passages.text: Первая — сам принципал. Полностью самообслуживаемая модель. Принципал просматривает каталог, выбирает, конфигурирует. Преимущество: полный контроль. Недостаток: принципал должен знать, что ему нужно, а это часто непонятно заранее.

passages.heading: Какой под-агент (или какие) должны её обработать
passages.text: Вторая — AI-рекомендация. На основе профиля принципала система предлагает конфигурацию. Принципал одобряет или модифицирует. Преимущество: меньше работы. Недостаток: AI может пропускать важные комбинации, которые сам принципал увидел бы.

passages.heading: Какой под-агент (или какие) должны её обработать
passages.text: Третья — человеческое наставничество. Опытный коллега или ментор помогает принципалу подобрать конфигурацию. Преимущество: глубокое понимание. Недостаток: требует доступа к ментору.

passages.heading: Какой под-агент (или какие) должны её обработать
passages.text: Это, кстати, точная аналогия с историей йога. Двадцать первый учитель не выбирал случайно. Он, скорее всего, имел собственного раннего наставника, который помог ему понять, какие специализации нужно изучать. И затем по мере роста сам корректировал выбор.

passages.heading: Какой под-агент (или какие) должны её обработать
passages.text: Риск фрагментации идентичности. Если у принципала десятки под-агентов, кто на самом деле представлен в его работе? Координатор? Под-агенты? Сам принципал?

passages.heading: Какой под-агент (или какие) должны её обработать
passages.text: Должна быть жёсткая граница: принципал является автором своей работы. Под-агенты — инструменты. Композитный агент — оркестратор этих инструментов. Идентичность работы остаётся за принципалом.

passages.heading: Какой под-агент (или какие) должны её обработать
passages.text: Риск зависимости от композиции. Если у принципала очень специфичный набор под-агентов, что произойдёт, если один из них перестанет поддерживаться? Нужна модульность и заменяемость.

passages.heading: Какой под-агент (или какие) должны её обработать
passages.text: Риск изоляции. Узкоспециализированные под-агенты могут не общаться с другими частями экосистемы. Поэтому интеграция с Тип 1 профессиональный коллега и другими типами критична.

passages.heading: Какой под-агент (или какие) должны её обработать
passages.text: Добавить Тип 1.5 или Тип 2 в типологию. Между «один шаблон для всей профессии» Тип 1 и «уникальный для индивидуума» Тип 5 — есть промежуточная категория.

passages.heading: Какой под-агент (или какие) должны её обработать
passages.text: Указать, как это меняет план развёртывания OKWF. Возможно, прежде чем строить Профессионального Коллегу-Агента для всей области социального права, стоит начать с набора узкоспециализированных под-агентов, которые потом могут быть скомпонованы в разные конфигурации.

passages.heading: Какой под-агент (или какие) должны её обработать
passages.text: Третий вариант — остановиться на этом наблюдении как самостоятельной заметке, не превращая её в полноценный документ. Иногда сильное наблюдение должно отлежаться, прежде чем принимать формальную форму. Семь документов за одну сессию — много. Может быть, шестой плюс эта заметка-расширение — достаточно.

passages.heading: Какой под-агент (или какие) должны её обработать
passages.text: Если выберете первый или второй вариант, я могу написать в следующем сообщении. Если третий — то этот ответ остаётся как ваша заметка к шестому документу, и работа сессии завершена с шестью полноценными артефактами плюс этим архитектурным расширением.

passages.heading: Какой под-агент (или какие) должны её обработать
passages.text: Honestly, я склоняюсь рекомендовать третий вариант. Шесть документов — это уже substantial intellectual product. Композитный Агент как концепция важен и заслуживает фиксации, но добавлять седьмой полный документ может быть перегрузкой. Эта заметка может служить архитектурным дополнением к шестому, которое вы можете в любой момент развить, если будет нужно.

passages.heading: Abstract
passages.text: We introduce the Double-Triangle Architecture for human-AI collaboration in distributed knowledge work. The central thesis: each human participant in modern AI-assisted workflows simultaneously occupies two roles — as conductor of personal AI assistants lower triangle, directed downward from human to assistants , and as performer coordinated by higher-level meta-agents upper triangle, directed upw

passages.heading: Abstract
passages.text: Existing systems implement only one triangle: personal assistants Cursor, Copilot, ChatGPT operate in the lower triangle only; multi-agent frameworks CrewAI, MetaGPT, AutoGen operate in the upper triangle only and typically replace humans rather than augment them. Neither paradigm captures the full structure of how humans will actually work alongside AI over the next decade.

passages.heading: Abstract
passages.text: 1. Formal specification of the Double-Triangle Architecture, including three inter-layer protocols and six architectural invariants 2. Reference implementation via Nautilus Portal Protocol NPP v1.1 , which provides the federated knowledge substrate required to support the architecture 3. Deployment paths for four concrete domains: humanities legal/medical/social , project management, open-source d

passages.heading: Abstract
passages.text: We also present empirical evidence from a 4-month single-person AI-assisted deployment producing 6,782 lines of production code across 13 adapters, a formal protocol specification, REST API, SDK, Docker containerization, and 60 passing tests — suggesting that single-person operations can achieve team-level output when the Double-Triangle substrate is properly instantiated.

passages.heading: Abstract
passages.text: We conclude with open questions on governance, consent, economics, and burnout dynamics, and invite research collaboration on these unsolved issues.

passages.heading: 1. Why Single-Triangle Models Are Incomplete
passages.text: Источник: MHTML‑снимок Вакансии в Anthropic по кластерам - Claude корень репозитория . Раздел диалога — paper «The Double-Triangle Architecture for Human-AI Collaboration».

passages.heading: 1.1. The Current Landscape
passages.text: The AI-assisted knowledge work field currently divides into two non-overlapping camps, each implementing only one triangle of the full architecture.

passages.heading: 1.1. The Current Landscape
passages.text: Lower-triangle-only systems. Personal AI assistants GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code, ChatGPT, Anthropic's Claude Desktop operate as extensions of individual knowledge workers. The human conducts, assistants execute. This paradigm has rapidly matured over 2023–2026 and is now mainstream. It answers: how does one person amplify their capacity with AI?

passages.heading: 1.1. The Current Landscape
passages.text: Upper-triangle-only systems. Multi-agent frameworks CrewAI, AutoGen, LangGraph, MetaGPT, ChatDev orchestrate multiple AI agents to complete complex tasks. Humans either serve as external observers or are absent from the execution loop. This paradigm answers: how do we automate entire workflows with AI?

passages.heading: 1.1. The Current Landscape
passages.text: Enterprise AI platforms Microsoft Copilot Enterprise, Google Workspace AI attempt to bridge these but do so through layer isolation — personal assistants and team-level orchestration exist as separate products without formal protocols between them.

passages.heading: 1.2. What Both Paradigms Miss
passages.text: Both single-triangle approaches share a structural blind spot: they assume humans exist in one role at a time. In reality, every knowledge worker simultaneously occupies both positions :

passages.heading: 1.2. What Both Paradigms Miss
passages.text: - A software engineer uses Copilot to write code lower triangle: human conducts assistant - At the same time, their team lead coordinates the engineer alongside five others toward a sprint goal upper triangle: meta-agent coordinates human

passages.heading: 1.2. What Both Paradigms Miss
passages.text: The engineer's decisions about what Copilot generates depend on the sprint context coming from upper triangle . The team lead's decisions about how to coordinate the engineer depend on what Copilot is producing coming from lower triangle . These two flows of information must be connected, yet in existing systems they are not.

passages.heading: 1.2. What Both Paradigms Miss
passages.text: This creates what we call the coordination gap : personal AI assistants don't know about team context, and team-level coordination tools don't know about assistant-generated artifacts. Information has to be manually translated by humans across this gap, constantly.

passages.heading: 1.3. The Rising Urgency
passages.text: As AI assistants become more capable, the coordination gap widens. When Copilot produced autocomplete in 2022, misalignment with team context was minor. When Claude Code produces entire modules in 2026, misalignment can destabilize architectural decisions across a team.

passages.heading: 1.3. The Rising Urgency
passages.text: The gap needs to be closed not through yet another centralized platform, but through a protocol — a way for the two triangles to negotiate through well-defined interfaces. This paper proposes such a protocol.

passages.heading: 1.3. The Rising Urgency

passages.heading: 2. The Double-Triangle Architecture
passages.text: Источник: MHTML‑снимок Вакансии в Anthropic по кластерам - Claude корень репозитория . Раздел диалога — paper «The Double-Triangle Architecture for Human-AI Collaboration».

passages.heading: 2.1. Topology
passages.text: where A 1, A 2, A 3 are AI assistants personalized to N's work. N conducts the triangle: tasks flow downward from N to assistants, results flow upward from assistants to N for integration.

passages.heading: 2.1. Topology
passages.text: where M is a meta-agent AI or human-augmented-AI and N 1, N 2, N 3 are human participants. M conducts the upper triangle: tasks flow downward from M to humans, deliverables flow upward from humans to M for integration.

passages.heading: 2.1. Topology
passages.text: Composition. Each human N is simultaneously the vertex of a lower triangle their own and a base node of an upper triangle their team's . Superimposing the two around this shared vertex produces a six-pointed star:

passages.heading: 2.1. Topology
passages.text: We refer to this as the Star of David topology , after the hexagram figure. The metaphor is deliberate: two superimposed triangles pointing in opposite directions, sharing common vertices.

passages.heading: 2.2. Fractal Self-Similarity
passages.text: The architecture is fractal: the meta-agent M itself participates as a Node in a higher-level upper triangle e.g., at the organization level . M has its own lower triangle of assistants supporting its coordination work. Recursively, any scale of organization can be represented as stacked Star-of-David topologies.

passages.heading: 2.2. Fractal Self-Similarity
passages.text: Formally, if Star k is the topology at level k : - Star 0 : individual human + personal assistants lower triangle only, no upper - Star 1 : individual embedded in team full Star, as depicted - Star 2 : team lead embedded in organization full Star at higher scale - Star n : recursively

passages.heading: 2.2. Fractal Self-Similarity
passages.text: This fractal property means the protocol for inter-layer communication scales naturally: the same three protocols introduced in §3 apply at every level.

passages.heading: 2.3. Six Architectural Invariants
passages.text: Invariant 1 — Dual Identity. Each human Node maintains two separate identity contexts: personal context their work-in-progress, drafts, notes, private patterns and team context their accepted deliverables, public roles, shared outputs . Personal context is richer; team context is filtered.

passages.heading: 2.3. Six Architectural Invariants
passages.text: Invariant 2 — Assistant Autonomy, Node Authority. Lower triangle assistants have broad autonomy to execute tasks within their scope, but the human Node retains final authority on what propagates upward to team context. Assistants cannot unilaterally publish to team-visible space.

passages.heading: 2.3. Six Architectural Invariants
passages.text: Invariant 3 — Meta-Agent Transparency, Not Omniscience. The meta-agent M can see all team-context data from all Nodes, but cannot see personal-context data of any Node. Its decisions must be explainable in terms of team context alone.

passages.heading: 2.3. Six Architectural Invariants
passages.text: Invariant 4 — Multi-Level Consensus. Conflicts can be resolved at three levels: within a Node's lower triangle between their assistants , between Nodes at the upper triangle, or at escalation points that involve human judgment. Each level uses the same consensus mechanism with different parameters.

passages.heading: 2.3. Six Architectural Invariants
passages.text: Invariant 5 — Distributed Audit Trail. Every cross-triangle communication is logged in at least two locations: the originating triangle and the receiving triangle. This enables reconstruction of decision chains without centralized logging.

passages.heading: 2.3. Six Architectural Invariants
passages.text: Invariant 6 — Fractal Compatibility. Any protocol valid at one level of the hierarchy must remain valid at all levels. This ensures the architecture scales from small teams Star 1 to large organizations Star n without protocol changes.

passages.heading: 2.3. Six Architectural Invariants

passages.heading: 3. Three Inter-Layer Protocols
passages.text: Источник: MHTML‑снимок Вакансии в Anthropic по кластерам - Claude корень репозитория . Раздел диалога — paper «The Double-Triangle Architecture for Human-AI Collaboration».

passages.heading: 3.1. Protocol 1 — Human Conducts Assistants
passages.text: Semantics. The Node issues tasks to assistants, reviews outputs, integrates results. This is the current state of personal AI assistant workflows and is well-developed.

passages.heading: 3.1. Protocol 1 — Human Conducts Assistants
passages.text: Message format. Natural language prompts with structured context file references, code selections, project files . Responses as text, code, or structured data.

passages.heading: 3.1. Protocol 1 — Human Conducts Assistants
passages.text: Extensions needed for Double-Triangle: Assistants must be aware of team context markers — annotations indicating which parts of their output affect team-visible deliverables versus purely personal work. This allows invariant 2 Assistant Autonomy, Node Authority to be enforced.

passages.heading: 3.2. Protocol 2 — Meta-Agent Coordinates Nodes
passages.text: Semantics. M assigns tasks to Nodes, receives deliverables, integrates team-level outputs. M does not see internal Node processes, only public deliverables.

passages.heading: 3.2. Protocol 2 — Meta-Agent Coordinates Nodes
passages.text: Existing implementations: Partial, fragmented. Jira with AI triage, Linear with AI suggestions, GitHub Projects with automation. None implement the full protocol, all require significant human management intervention.

passages.heading: 3.2. Protocol 2 — Meta-Agent Coordinates Nodes
passages.text: Message format. Structured tasks with: - Description - Deliverable specification what constitutes "done" - Dependencies on other Nodes' deliverables - Deadline - Priority - Assignee

passages.heading: 3.2. Protocol 2 — Meta-Agent Coordinates Nodes
passages.text: Failure modes: Task assignment mismatches wrong Node, wrong skill , deadline conflicts, scope creep, dependency deadlocks. These are classical project management challenges adapted to AI orchestration.

passages.heading: 3.2. Protocol 2 — Meta-Agent Coordinates Nodes
passages.text: Extensions needed for Double-Triangle: M must respect invariant 3 Meta-Agent Transparency, Not Omniscience — decisions must cite only team-context reasoning, never reference Nodes' personal data. Requires careful design to prevent information leakage.

passages.heading: 3.3. Protocol 3 — Assistant-to-Meta Negotiation
passages.text: Semantics. This is the novel protocol . When an assistant in N's lower triangle requires information or coordination that involves other Nodes, it does not ping those Nodes directly. Instead, it issues a structured query that travels: A → N → M → N' → A' → response back through the chain.

passages.heading: 3.3. Protocol 3 — Assistant-to-Meta Negotiation
passages.text: Existing implementations: None in production systems. Closest analog: GitHub Copilot Workspace can see other team members' public code but cannot negotiate with their assistants. Anthropic's Managed Agents API moves toward this but does not implement full cross-triangle negotiation.

passages.heading: 3.3. Protocol 3 — Assistant-to-Meta Negotiation
passages.text: - Query messages: "Assistant requires information X; X is outside current Node's scope; routing request via meta-agent" - Notification messages: "Assistant detected conflict with team context; escalating to meta-agent for resolution" - Proposal messages: "Assistant proposes decision D affecting multiple Nodes; requesting meta-agent consensus routing"

passages.heading: 3.3. Protocol 3 — Assistant-to-Meta Negotiation
passages.text: Routing semantics. Messages are routed by the meta-agent based on: - Ownership: which Node owns the relevant artifact - Expertise: which Node has the required domain knowledge - Availability: which Node is currently responsive

passages.heading: 3.3. Protocol 3 — Assistant-to-Meta Negotiation
passages.text: Failure modes: Routing loops, context fragmentation details lost in translation , escalation spirals where every conflict reaches human review. These are genuinely unsolved and require empirical development.

passages.heading: 3.3. Protocol 3 — Assistant-to-Meta Negotiation
passages.text: Why this protocol matters. Without Protocol 3, humans become routing bottlenecks. Every cross-Node coordination requires humans to manually translate from their assistants' findings to team context, wait for replies, translate back. This adds hours or days to each interaction. Protocol 3 reduces this to minutes or seconds.

passages.heading: 3.4. Protocol Interactions
passages.text: Escalation chain. Assistant detects issue Protocol 3 → M → M evaluates internal → M modifies task assignment Protocol 2 → Node receives updated task Protocol 2 → Node redirects assistant Protocol 1 .

passages.heading: 3.4. Protocol Interactions
passages.text: Context propagation. M updates team context Protocol 2 to all Nodes → Each Node propagates relevant updates to their assistants Protocol 1 → Assistants adjust behavior accordingly.

passages.heading: 3.4. Protocol Interactions
passages.text: Cross-Node handoff. Assistant of N 1 completes artifact Protocol 1 → Node N 1 reviews and approves Protocol 1 → N 1 submits to M Protocol 2 → M routes to N 2 Protocol 2 → N 2's assistant picks up Protocol 1 .

passages.heading: 4. Nautilus Portal as Reference Substrate
passages.text: The Double-Triangle Architecture requires a substrate capable of: - Representing diverse knowledge sources uniformly for assistants to query across Nodes - Providing distributed, persistent memory for context continuity - Supporting multi-level consensus for conflict resolution - Enabling federated queries for Protocol 3 routing

passages.heading: 4. Nautilus Portal as Reference Substrate
passages.text: Nautilus Portal Protocol NPP v1.1 was designed for knowledge federation but provides exactly these properties. We propose NPP as the reference substrate for Double-Triangle implementations.

passages.heading: 4.1. NPP Components Mapped to Double-Triangle Requirements
passages.text: Adapters NPP = interface between participants and shared space. In Double-Triangle, each assistant can read and write through the same adapter mechanism used by any participant, providing uniform cross-triangle access.

passages.heading: 4.1. NPP Components Mapped to Double-Triangle Requirements
passages.text: PortalEntry structure NPP = unified unit of knowledge. In Double-Triangle, this represents tasks, deliverables, context updates, and notifications uniformly, enabling a single mechanism for all inter-layer communication.

passages.heading: 4.1. NPP Components Mapped to Double-Triangle Requirements
passages.text: Consensus model NPP = conflict resolution between sources. In Double-Triangle, consensus operates at three levels intra-Node between assistants, inter-Node, meta-level , all using the same mechanism with different scope.

passages.heading: 4.1. NPP Components Mapped to Double-Triangle Requirements
passages.text: Q6 coordinate space NPP = unified addressing for concepts. In Double-Triangle, Q6 addresses tasks and deliverables uniformly across domains, enabling cross-Node task similarity queries.

passages.heading: 4.1. NPP Components Mapped to Double-Triangle Requirements
passages.text: Bridges NPP = formal links between participants' domains. In Double-Triangle, bridges formalize responsibility boundaries between Nodes "authentication is N 1's domain, authorization is N 2's, interface is: token format" .

passages.heading: 4.1. NPP Components Mapped to Double-Triangle Requirements
passages.text: Compatibility levels NPP = graduated participation. In Double-Triangle, this allows Nodes to join teams with minimal setup Level 0–1 and mature over time to full integration Level 3 .

passages.heading: 4.1. NPP Components Mapped to Double-Triangle Requirements
passages.text: Federation over merging NPP principle = preserve source autonomy. In Double-Triangle, this ensures Nodes remain functional without the meta-agent; M augments coordination but does not replace Node autonomy.

passages.heading: 4.2. Required Extensions to NPP for Double-Triangle
passages.text: Extension 1: Agent Registry. NPP v1.1 registers repositories. Double-Triangle requires registering agents AI assistants and meta-agents as first-class participants. Agents have identities, capabilities, scope of authority, and audit trails.

passages.heading: 4.2. Required Extensions to NPP for Double-Triangle
passages.text: Extension 2: Task Protocol. NPP v1.1 supports queries but not tasks. Double-Triangle requires formal task objects: task assignment, acceptance, completion, rejection, reassignment.

passages.heading: 4.2. Required Extensions to NPP for Double-Triangle
passages.text: Extension 3: Role Protocol. NPP v1.1 has no concept of roles. Double-Triangle requires roles to be first-class: "this Node is responsible for X", "this assistant handles Y". Role assignments constrain Protocol 3 routing.

passages.heading: 4.2. Required Extensions to NPP for Double-Triangle
passages.text: These extensions are additive — they do not break NPP v1.1 compatibility. A Double-Triangle implementation is an NPP v1.1 implementation plus these extensions.

passages.heading: 4.3. Empirical Evidence from Nautilus Reference Implementation
passages.text: - 6,782 lines of Python, 13 adapters, 60 tests passing, 0 mypy errors - 7 knowledge repositories federated info1, pro2, meta, data2, data7, infosystems, ai agents - 5 extended adapters enabling federation of external sources Obsidian vaults, arXiv papers, GitHub-topic repos, JSONL files, self-declaring repos via AutoAdapter - Zero external dependencies Python stdlib only - Full REST API, MCP wrapp

passages.heading: 4.3. Empirical Evidence from Nautilus Reference Implementation
passages.text: This demonstrates that NPP can be implemented by a single developer in 4 months, providing a practical foundation for Double-Triangle deployments.

passages.heading: 5. Pattern Library as Bridge Between Triangles
passages.text: Источник: MHTML‑снимок Вакансии в Anthropic по кластерам - Claude корень репозитория . Раздел диалога — paper «The Double-Triangle Architecture for Human-AI Collaboration».

passages.heading: 5.1. The Problem of Shared Knowledge
passages.text: Double-Triangle systems face a fundamental question: how do assistants in different Nodes' lower triangles share knowledge about best practices, conventions, and reusable patterns, without each Node privately replicating this knowledge?

passages.heading: 5.1. The Problem of Shared Knowledge
passages.text: Centralized shared knowledge company wiki, organization playbook has known problems: it stales, it duplicates with external sources, and it creates single points of failure.

passages.heading: 5.2. Pattern Library Architecture
passages.text: Tier 1 — Public Patterns. Repositories of abstract patterns: methodologies Scrum, Kanban, DDD , legal norms SGB statutes, EU directives , templates pull request templates, meeting formats , best practices, antipatterns. These are shared across many teams and organizations.

passages.heading: 5.2. Pattern Library Architecture
passages.text: Tier 2 — Private Instances. Concrete applications of patterns within specific contexts: a team's actual sprint, a lawyer's actual case, a developer's actual deployment. These are Node-specific and often confidential.

passages.heading: 5.2. Pattern Library Architecture
passages.text: Inheritance relationship. Each private instance inherits from one or more public patterns. An instance can override specific parts of a pattern while retaining the overall structure.

passages.heading: 5.3. Three Types of Bridges
passages.text: Contribution bridge. Private instance generates anonymized pattern to contribute back to public library. Direction: instance → pattern through anonymization pipeline .

passages.heading: 5.3. Three Types of Bridges
passages.text: - Start of work: instance inherits from patterns use existing knowledge - During work: instance cites authorities ground work in source material - After work: instance contributes back compound shared knowledge

passages.heading: 5.4. Anonymization as Contribution Mechanism
passages.text: 1. PII detection names, dates, addresses, identifiers 2. Replacement with type-consistent placeholders 3. Manual verification automated anonymization is insufficient 4. Structural metadata addition pattern type, outcome, applicability 5. Publication to public tier

passages.heading: 5.4. Anonymization as Contribution Mechanism
passages.text: This pipeline enables Tier 2 instances to generate Tier 1 patterns while preserving privacy. Anonymization becomes the compounding mechanism for shared knowledge.

passages.heading: 5.5. Why This Architecture Is Critical for Double-Triangle
passages.text: Without pattern library architecture: - Assistants in N 1's lower triangle and N 2's lower triangle cannot share knowledge - Cross-Node learning requires explicit human coordination - Team knowledge does not compound with use

passages.heading: 5.5. Why This Architecture Is Critical for Double-Triangle
passages.text: With pattern library architecture: - Assistants can query public patterns before executing tasks Protocol 1 - Meta-agent can route tasks based on pattern fit Protocol 2 - Nodes can contribute back after successful execution closing the loop

passages.heading: 5.5. Why This Architecture Is Critical for Double-Triangle
passages.text: The pattern library is the glue that binds the upper and lower triangles into a coherent system where knowledge flows efficiently between levels.

passages.heading: 6. Four Deployment Domains
passages.text: The Double-Triangle Architecture is domain-agnostic but benefits from concrete deployment analysis. We describe four domains where the architecture applies naturally.

passages.heading: 6.1. Humanities Domain (Legal, Medical, Social)
passages.text: Lower triangle contents. Assistants specialized for: - Legal research case law, statute lookup - Document drafting Widerspruch, Klage, petitions - Compliance checking GDPR, medical confidentiality - Timeline tracking deadlines, Fristwahrung

passages.heading: 6.1. Humanities Domain (Legal, Medical, Social)
passages.text: Concrete deployment. An individual the first author, svend4 currently engages with Sozialgericht Dresden on cases S 6 SO 58/26 ER and S 7 SO 99/25. Personal workflow already exhibits lower triangle structure Claude Code for technical documents, Claude Sonnet for German legal drafting . Upper triangle would emerge when other advocates working on related cases coordinate through shared anonymized pa

passages.heading: 6.1. Humanities Domain (Legal, Medical, Social)
passages.text: Regulatory considerations. GDPR Article 5 data minimization , § 203 StGB professional confidentiality , UrhG § 5 public domain status of statutes and court decisions . All compatible with Double-Triangle if anonymization pipeline operates correctly.

passages.heading: 6.2. Project Management Domain
passages.text: Lower triangle contents. Assistants specialized for: - Code generation and review Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code - Design ideation Figma AI, sketch tools - Deployment automation Terraform AI, kubectl-ai - Test generation property-based test synthesis

passages.heading: 6.2. Project Management Domain
passages.text: Existing partial implementations. Jira AI, Linear AI, GitHub Projects automation — all provide fragments of this architecture but lack Protocol 3.

passages.heading: 6.2. Project Management Domain
passages.text: Business opportunity. Organizations currently spend 20–30% of engineering budget on middle management. A Double-Triangle implementation that replaces some coordination functions with AI meta-agents while keeping humans in the engineer role could significantly alter organizational economics.

passages.heading: 6.3. Open-Source Development Domain
passages.text: Lower triangle contents. Per-participant assistants for: - Contribution drafting PRs, issues, documentation - Code review automated checks, suggestion generation - Community moderation anti-spam, tone analysis

passages.heading: 6.3. Open-Source Development Domain
passages.text: Upper triangle contents. Meta-agent handling: - Triage and routing of incoming contributions - Release planning and coordination - Security vulnerability coordination - Community health monitoring

passages.heading: 6.3. Open-Source Development Domain
passages.text: Pattern library examples. Governance templates BDFL, foundation-based, consensus , contribution guidelines, release playbooks, security advisory formats, code of conduct templates.

passages.heading: 6.3. Open-Source Development Domain
passages.text: Novel opportunity. Open-source projects traditionally lack scalable coordination. A Double-Triangle deployment could enable small maintainer teams to manage much larger contributor communities without proportional coordination overhead.

passages.heading: 6.4. Generic Knowledge Work Domain
passages.text: Lower triangle contents. Assistants for: - Literature review and synthesis - Draft generation and revision - Data analysis and visualization - Citation management

passages.heading: 6.4. Generic Knowledge Work Domain
passages.text: Upper triangle contents. Meta-agent coordinating: - Research group collaboration - Multi-author paper writing - Conference/workshop organization - Grant application coordination

passages.heading: 6.4. Generic Knowledge Work Domain
passages.text: Observation. This domain is perhaps the broadest application of Double-Triangle architecture. Most modern knowledge workers could potentially benefit from this structure once mature tools exist.
